The Stage 2 BIT is executed after the operating system is booted and is not part of the Bootstrap program.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines the Built-In Test context for the DPU-BOOT CSC by specifying that Stage 1 BIT is part of the Bootstrap program and includes CPU and DRAM tests. This directly supports the higher-level logging requirement because it identifies the BIT activities whose detected failures would be relevant for DPU-BOOT handling and logging to the SYSTEM_BLOCK. The relationship is a refinement of the source and scope of BIT failures within the boot process.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall log detected BIT failures to the SYSTEM_BLOCK.
lower_level_requirement: DRAM BITPart of the memory is tested in Boot Sequence 1, and part of the memory is tested during Boot Sequence 2. During Boot Sequence 1, ? KB of DRAM is tested before the Bootstrap is copied to this area. During Boot Sequence 2, the remaining memory is tested in ? KB blocks. The DRAM BIT first writes the address of each word in a block to that word in the block. Then the test flushes the cache and reads back the entire block. If a single-bit error occurs on the read-back, the location is read again. If another single-bit error occurs, the test assumes a hard error and marks the whole block bad. If a multiple-bit error occurs, the whole block is marked bad. If the value read back does not match the address, the whole block is marked bad. This same process is repeated with the ones complement of the address. The Bootstrap stores the results of the DRAM BIT in EEPROM as a series of x consecutive y-bit words. Each bit in a result word represents the result of testing a ? KB block of DRAM. These bits are mapped to DRAM by proceeding from least-significant bit (LSb) to most-significant bit (MSb) as the addresses of the memory blocks increase. A set bit indicates that a block of DRAM has failed. A clear bit indicates that a block of DRAM has passed the test.
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement defines a specific Built-In Test for DRAM, including how failures are detected and encoded as test results. By specifying that failed DRAM blocks are recorded persistently in EEPROM as BIT result words, it operationalizes the higher-level requirement to log detected BIT failures to a system storage area. The semantic link is that detected memory BIT failures are captured and stored as failure records, directly supporting the required logging behavior.

higher_level_requirement: The DPU-BOOT CSC shall log detected BIT failures to the SYSTEM_BLOCK.

The DPU-RTOS uses the results of the memory test to exclude memory segments with bit errors from the system memory pool. The Bootstrap constructs a bit map which effectively implements a list of failed memory blocks during the bootstrap built-in test. A set of functions have been created to utilize this bit map to exclude failed memory blocks from the VxWorks system memory pool. The system memory pool is used by VxWorks to allocate memory dynamically. In addition, a linked list of good memory segments is created for use by the EDAC Memory Scrubber. These functions are called from the usrInit() and usrRoot() functions in usrConfig.c. The dramInit() function must be called prior to kernelInit() in usrInit(). The dramBuildMemPool() function is called just prior to initialization of filesystems and drivers in usrRoot().
label: trace
rationale: The lower-level requirement operationalizes handling of bootstrap memory BIT results by describing how failed DRAM blocks detected during the bootstrap built-in test are recorded as a bitmap and persisted in EEPROM. This directly supports the higher-level requirement to log detected BIT failures, because the detected memory failures are captured in a structured record for later system use. Although it focuses on DRAM failures and their exclusion from the memory pool, the storage of the test results and failed block list is a concrete implementation of logging BIT failures.
